description: CS50 SQL exercises on the bundled databases (user-supplied prompts, gold SQL). Paraphrases test wording robustness.

cases.question: Show me just the titles from the original season of Cyberchase.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT title FROM episodes WHERE season = 1

cases.question: For each season, what was its first episode? Give me the season and title.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT season, title FROM episodes WHERE episode_in_season = 1

cases.question: What's the PBS production code for Hackerized!?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT production_code FROM episodes WHERE title = 'Hackerized!'
paraphrases: Find Hackerized! and tell me its PBS code.
I need the internal code corresponding to the episode named Hackerized!.
Which production identifier belongs to Hackerized!?
Can you look up Hackerized! for me? Just its production code.

cases.question: Which episodes don't have a topic assigned yet? Just give me their titles.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT title FROM episodes WHERE topic IS NULL

cases.question: What episode aired on December 31, 2004?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT title FROM episodes WHERE air_date = '2004-12-31'

cases.question: I only want the titles of season 6 episodes that actually came out during 2007.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT title FROM episodes WHERE season = 6 AND air_date BETWEEN '2007-01-01' AND '2007-12-31'

cases.question: Show me the title and topic of every episode that teaches something about fractions.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT title, topic FROM episodes WHERE topic LIKE '%fractions%'
paraphrases: Show me everything about episodes whose lessons involve fractions.
Which episodes deal with fractions? I need their names and topics.
I'm only interested in fraction-related episodes. Give me title plus topic.
Can you pull the episode names together with their topics wherever fractions are being taught?
Forget the other subjects; what Cyberchase episodes cover fractions?

cases.question: How many episodes came out from 2018 through 2023, including both years?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM episodes WHERE air_date BETWEEN '2018-01-01' AND '2023-12-31'

cases.question: How many episodes were released during the first six years, 2002 through 2007?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM episodes WHERE air_date BETWEEN '2002-01-01' AND '2007-12-31'

cases.question: Give me each episode's id, title and production code, sorted from the earliest production code onward.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT id, title, production_code FROM episodes ORDER BY production_code ASC

cases.question: I only care about season 5. Give me its episode titles backwards alphabetically.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT title FROM episodes WHERE season = 5 ORDER BY title DESC

cases.question: How many different episode titles are there?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT title) FROM episodes

cases.question: Give me the names and cities of Massachusetts public schools, but don't include charter schools.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name, city FROM schools WHERE type = 'Public School'

cases.question: Which districts aren't operating anymore?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM districts WHERE name LIKE '%(non-op)'

cases.question: What's the average amount districts spend per pupil?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT AVG(per_pupil_expenditure) FROM expenditures

cases.question: Which 10 cities have the most public schools? Show the city and count, biggest first, alphabetically for ties.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE type='Public School' GROUP BY city ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, city ASC LIMIT 10

cases.question: Show cities that have no more than three public schools. Give me city and number of schools.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM schools WHERE type='Public School' GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) <= 3 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, city ASC

cases.question: Which schools had a perfect graduation rate?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT schools.name FROM schools JOIN graduation_rates ON schools.id = graduation_rates.school_id WHERE graduation_rates.graduated = 100

cases.question: What schools belong to the district called Cambridge?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT schools.name FROM schools JOIN districts ON schools.district_id = districts.id WHERE districts.name = 'Cambridge'

cases.question: Give me every school district together with its pupil count.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT districts.name, expenditures.pupils FROM districts JOIN expenditures ON districts.id = expenditures.district_id

cases.question: Which district has the smallest number of pupils? Preserve ties.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT districts.name FROM districts JOIN expenditures ON districts.id=expenditures.district_id WHERE expenditures.pupils = (SELECT MIN(pupils) FROM expenditures)

cases.question: What are the ten public school districts that spend the most per student?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT districts.name, expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure FROM districts JOIN expenditures ON districts.id=expenditures.district_id WHERE districts.type='Public School District' ORDER BY expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure DESC LIMIT 10

cases.question: Show every school with its graduation rate and the amount its district spends per pupil. Put the highest-spending schools first, and break spending ties alphabetically by school.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT schools.name, expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure, graduation_rates.graduated
                     FROM schools JOIN districts ON schools.district_id = districts.id
                     JOIN expenditures ON districts.id = expenditures.district_id
                     JOIN graduation_rates ON schools.id = graduation_rates.school_id
                     ORDER BY expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure DESC, schools.name ASC

cases.question: Find public school districts that spend more per pupil than the statewide district average and also have a higher-than-average percentage of exemplary teachers. Show district, expenditure and exemplary percentage. Rank exemplary percentage highest first, then expenditure highest first.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT districts.name, expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure, staff_evaluations.exemplary
                     FROM districts JOIN expenditures ON districts.id = expenditures.district_id
                     JOIN staff_evaluations ON districts.id = staff_evaluations.district_id
                     WHERE districts.type = 'Public School District'
                     AND expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure > (SELECT AVG(per_pupil_expenditure) FROM expenditures)
                     AND staff_evaluations.exemplary > (SELECT AVG(exemplary) FROM staff_evaluations)
                     ORDER BY staff_evaluations.exemplary DESC, expenditures.per_pupil_expenditure DESC

cases.question: How did the average MLB salary change over time? Give me year and average salary rounded to two decimals, newest year first.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT year, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM salaries GROUP BY year ORDER BY year DESC

cases.question: Show me Cal Ripken's salary history, newest year first.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT salaries.year, salaries.salary FROM players JOIN salaries ON players.id = salaries.player_id
                     WHERE players.first_name = 'Cal' AND players.last_name = 'Ripken' ORDER BY salaries.year DESC

cases.question: Give me the yearly home-run history for the Ken Griffey who was born in 1969. Newest season first.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT performances.year, performances.HR FROM players JOIN performances ON players.id = performances.player_id
                     WHERE players.first_name = 'Ken' AND players.last_name = 'Griffey' AND players.birth_year = 1969
                     ORDER BY performances.year DESC

cases.question: Who were the 50 lowest-paid players in 2001? Show first name, last name and salary. Cheapest first. Resolve equal salaries by first name, last name, then player id.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT players.first_name, players.last_name, salaries.salary FROM players
                     JOIN salaries ON players.id = salaries.player_id WHERE salaries.year = 2001
                     ORDER BY salaries.salary ASC, players.first_name ASC, players.last_name ASC, players.id ASC LIMIT 50

cases.question: Which teams did Satchel Paige play for? Don't repeat a team.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT teams.name FROM players JOIN performances ON players.id = performances.player_id
                     JOIN teams ON performances.team_id = teams.id WHERE players.first_name = 'Satchel' AND players.last_name = 'Paige'

cases.question: Which five teams produced the most total hits in 2001? Show the team and total hits, highest first.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT teams.name, SUM(performances.H) FROM teams JOIN performances ON teams.id = performances.team_id
                     WHERE performances.year = 2001 GROUP BY teams.id ORDER BY SUM(performances.H) DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: Who received the highest salary in the entire database? Give me the player's first and last name.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT players.first_name, players.last_name FROM players JOIN salaries ON players.id = salaries.player_id
                     WHERE salaries.salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM salaries)
paraphrases: Who got paid more than anyone else ever?
Who's the highest-paid player in this data?
Find whoever received the biggest single salary.
Which player has the all-time maximum salary?
I just want the name of whoever got the largest paycheck.

cases.question: What salary did the top home-run hitter of 2001 receive that year?
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT salaries.salary FROM salaries JOIN performances
                     ON salaries.player_id = performances.player_id AND salaries.year = performances.year
                     WHERE performances.year = 2001 AND performances.HR =
                     (SELECT MAX(HR) FROM performances WHERE year = 2001)

cases.question: Which five teams had the lowest average salary in 2001? Give me team and average salary rounded to two decimals.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT teams.name, ROUND(AVG(salaries.salary), 2) FROM teams JOIN salaries
                     ON teams.id = salaries.team_id WHERE salaries.year = 2001 GROUP BY teams.id
                     ORDER BY ROUND(AVG(salaries.salary), 2) ASC LIMIT 5

cases.question: For every player and year, show first name, last name, salary, home runs and year. Make sure salary and performance refer to the same year.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT players.first_name, players.last_name, salaries.salary, performances.HR, salaries.year
                     FROM players JOIN salaries ON players.id = salaries.player_id
                     JOIN performances ON players.id = performances.player_id AND salaries.year = performances.year
                     ORDER BY players.id ASC, salaries.year DESC, performances.HR DESC, salaries.salary DESC

cases.question: Who were the ten cheapest players per hit in 2001? Ignore players with zero hits. Show first name, last name and dollars per hit.
cases.gold_sql:
SELECT players.first_name, players.last_name, salaries.salary / performances.H
                     FROM players JOIN salaries ON players.id = salaries.player_id
                     JOIN performances ON players.id = performances.player_id AND salaries.year = performances.year
                     WHERE salaries.year = 2001 AND performances.H > 0
                     ORDER BY salaries.salary / performances.H ASC, players.first_name ASC, players.last_name ASC LIMIT 10

cases.question: Which players are simultaneously among the ten cheapest per hit and the ten cheapest per RBI in 2001?
cases.gold_sql:
WITH costs AS (
                         SELECT players.id, players.first_name, players.last_name,
                                salaries.salary * 1.0 / performances.H AS per_hit,
                                salaries.salary * 1.0 / performances.RBI AS per_rbi
                         FROM players JOIN salaries ON players.id = salaries.player_id
                         JOIN performances ON players.id = performances.player_id AND salaries.year = performances.year
                         WHERE salaries.year = 2001 AND performances.H > 0 AND performances.RBI > 0
                     ), hit_top AS (SELECT id FROM costs ORDER BY per_hit ASC LIMIT 10),
                     rbi_top AS (SELECT id FROM costs ORDER BY per_rbi ASC LIMIT 10)
                     SELECT DISTINCT costs.first_name, costs.last_name FROM costs
                     JOIN hit_top USING(id) JOIN rbi_top USING(id)
